**Steroidkurer** (steroid courses) are specific, defined treatment regimens involving the corticosteroids prednisolone or prednisone, tracked within the Danish national health registries to monitor the quality of care for patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) [^src1]. A treatment is officially classified as a *steroidkur* when the total redeemed quantity of these medications reaches at least 500 mg within a three-month period [^src1]. This threshold is designed to capture a standard treatment course, which typically begins at a 40 mg dose and tapers down by 5 mg per week [^src1].

These treatment courses are the central focus of [[indikator-4|Indikator 4]], a national quality indicator in Denmark [^src1]. Because prolonged or high-dose steroid use carries significant risks, including bone density loss, Indikator 4 measures the proportion of IBD patients over the age of 50 who receive a DEXA scan (bone density screening) in conjunction with their steroid treatments [^src1]. 

During the most recent reporting period, the national registry recorded a total of 973 steroid courses administered to 861 unique patients [^src1]. The rigorous tracking of these courses reflects a broader, continuous national effort to ensure evidence-based, standardized follow-up for IBD patients, particularly when they are prescribed potentially risky medications like systemic steroids.

## Mentions
- **Page 27:** "Steroidbehandling omfatter indløste recepter for prednisolon og prednison i lægemiddelstatistikregisteret (ATC-koder: H02AB06/07). Det defineres som en kur, når den/de indløste recepters samlede varemængde er mindst 500 mg (standardkur svarende til 40mg med nedtrapning 5 mg pr. uge)." [^src1]
